title: R' Yeiva Saba
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.
copyright: English translation and editorial notes © 2026 Joshua Waxman. All rights reserved.
paragraphs: He is mentioned several times in the Zohar. In Bereishit 59a, a man harbored doubts about the commandment of circumcision. Rabbi Yeiva Saba fixed his eyes on him, and he became a heap of bones. Elsewhere the Zohar mentions “the aggadah of the school of Rabbi Yeiva Saba.” This is what Seder HaDorot means in its entry Rav Yeiva, where it writes “Rabbi Yeiva Saba והת׳”: its intention is “and he is a tanna,” because he is mentioned in the Zohar.[^1]

notes.text: Saba means “the Elder.” Hyman’s second locator is printed האינו רצ.; רצ. denotes folio 290a, but the section name is uncertain. The print has והת׳ where the accepted Hebrew transcription has והח׳. Hyman explains the abbreviation as והוא תנא, “and he is a tanna,” inferring this description from Yeiva’s appearance in the Zohar.
